content: 1. Entrectinib metabolism is influenced by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or consider alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and adjust the dose accordingly. Discontinuation of the CYP3A4 inhibitor may require an increase in entrectinib dosage in the absence of drug-related toxicities. 2. Itraconazole and itraconazole coadministration with itraconazole increases the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs to mitigate the risk of QT prolongation. 3. Itraconazole increases enzalutamide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while enzalutamide decreases itraconazole levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs to prevent significant drug interactions. 4. Itraconazole increases eplerenone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, which may elevate the risk of hyperkalemia and hypotension. Coadministration is contraindicated. 5. Itraconazole increases erdafitinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions and consider dose adjustments. Discontinuation of the inhibitor may necessitate an increase in erdafitinib dosage. 6. Itraconazole increases ergoloid mesylates and ergotamine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, raising the risk of ergotism, cerebral ischemia, and extremity ischemia. Coadministration is contraindicated. 7. Itraconazole and eribulin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs to reduce the risk of QT prolongation. 8. Itraconazole increases erlotinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for severe adverse reactions such as diarrhea or skin reactions, and adjust the erlotinib dose in 50 mg decrements if needed. 9. Erythromycin base increases itraconazole levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Itraconazole also increases erythromycin base levels. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 10. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases itraconazole levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Itraconazole also increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 11. Erythromycin lactobionate increases itraconazole levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Itraconazole also increases erythromycin lactobionate levels. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 12. Erythromycin stearate increases itraconazole levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Itraconazole also increases erythromycin stearate levels. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 13. Itraconazole increases escitalopram levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases itraconazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 15. Esomeprazole decreases itraconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 16. Itraconazole increases estradiol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Itraconazole increases ethinyl estradiol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. CYP3A4 inhibitors like itraconazole may elevate plasma hormone levels. 18. Itraconazole increases etoposide levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Itraconazole increases everolimus levels via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Coadministration is not recommended during and for two weeks after itraconazole treatment. 20. Famotidine decreases itraconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 21. Fedratinib increases itraconazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the fedratinib dose to 200 mg/day. If the inhibitor is discontinued, increase the fedratinib dose to 300 mg/day for two weeks, then to 400 mg/day as tolerated. 22. Itraconazole increases felbamate levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 23. Felodipine increases itraconazole levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Itraconazole also increases felodipine levels. Coadministration is contraindicated due to additive negative inotropic effects and itraconazole's inhibition of calcium channel blocker metabolism. 24. Itraconazole increases fentanyl levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust the fentanyl dose until stable effects are achieved. 25. Itraconazole increases fesoterodine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated, especially in patients with renal or hepatic impairment, due to the risk of potentially fatal adverse events. 26. Itraconazole decreases fexinidazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, increasing the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 27. Itraconazole increases fexofenadine levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 28. Itraconazole increases finasteride levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Itraconazole increases finerenone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 30. Itraconazole and fingolimod both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Itraconazole and flecainide both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 32. Itraconazole increases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope. 33. Itraconazole and fluconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Fluconazole increases itraconazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 34. Flucytosine enhances itraconazole effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 35. Itraconazole increases fludrocortisone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Itraconazole increases flunisolide inhaled levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Itraconazole and fluoxetine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Itraconazole and fluphenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Itraconazole increases flurazepam levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Itraconazole increases fluticasone furoate levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic corticosteroid exposure. 41. Itraconazole increases fluticasone inhaled levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic corticosteroid exposure. 42. Itraconazole increases fluticasone intranasal levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic corticosteroid adverse effects, including Cushing-type symptoms. 43. Itraconazole and fluvoxamine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Itraconazole and formoterol both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Itraconazole increases fosamprenavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs.
